A MUTATION THAT FAILED NOTHING IS THE REASON THE PHASE CHECK IS PROVEN. Removing the phaseId comparison broke no test at first, because briefId is `phaseId@head` and the brief comparison caught the wrong-phase fixture instead. A guard whose proof another guard also satisfies is not proven, so a laundered record — foreign phaseId with a truthful-looking briefId — was constructed to isolate it. Only then did the mutation bite. All four mutations (phase comparison, briefId comparison, write ordering, lock exists discriminator) now fail their own proof and no other; the ordering mutation fails four proofs at once, which is what makes the ordering load-bearing rather than incidental.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 4 IS DECIDED, NOT DEFERRED SILENTLY. The approved plan requires the unbounded configured-check timeout carried forward from the worker-lifecycle phase to be DECIDED AND RECORDED. It is recorded here as a deliberate deferral: `runCheck` (projectos/agent/src/loop/verification.ts) passes no timeoutMs, and sys.exec (src/system.ts) applies a timeout only when one is given, so a configured validator that hangs holds the ProjectOS process indefinitely. Output is bounded; execution time is not. Confirmed still true at this subject by reading current source rather than by trusting the earlier note. A correct fix needs a governed execution/config timeout contract — a committed field beside the worker configuration, gated by the same committed-execution check — not an ad-hoc constant introduced inside session recovery, and no partial mechanism is introduced here. The item is DEFERRED as explicit technical debt. It is not authority bypass, not data corruption, not protected-action leakage and not false recovery: a hang is the ABSENCE of an interruption, which is the opposite of what this phase recovers from. Under the established phase-extension law it does not block closure.

WHAT THIS PHASE ACTUALLY PROVED, in one sentence: a resume must describe the run it claims to continue — same session, same phase, same worker, same kind, and the same brief, so that the same phase at a moved head is refused too — a refused resume no longer damages the record it failed to recover, the owner-receipt lock says which of its two failures happened so its operator remedy is reachable, and what the last run left behind is reported truthfully, including when the answer is that it cannot be determined, while remaining evidence that decides nothing.
